issues.evidence: RTL8153B REGOUT (U2 pin 28, the switching/LDO 1.0V regulator output) connects only to C11 (10u to GND). The +1V0 net (AVDD10 pins 3/8/37, U3VDD10 pin 14, U2VDD10 pin 19, DVDD10 pin 34, plus C7/C8 and an In3.Cu plane) has no source, and REGOUT is not connected to it in the schematic or the PCB. There is also no inductor anywhere on the board. Datasheet section 6.14: 'REGOUT must be connected only to DVDD10, AVDD10, U3VDD10, and U2VDD10'.
issues.why_it_matters: The chip's 1.0V core, PHY and USB rails are unpowered, so the adapter cannot work. In switching mode, REGOUT also needs a series inductor before the 1.0V rail.

issues.evidence: U2 pin 25 (EEDI/SPISDI/ENSWREG) is marked no-connect. The datasheet describes ENSWREG as a power-on latch pin: 3.3V enables the switching regulator, 0V selects LDO mode or an external 1.0V. No default or internal pull is documented.
issues.why_it_matters: The regulator mode is undefined at power-up. If switching mode latches with no inductor on REGOUT, the 1.0V supply misbehaves. The pin should be strapped to the intended mode.

issues.evidence: U2 pin 26 VDDREG33 ('Digital 3.3V Power Supply for Switching/LDO Regulator') is left no-connect. VDDREG5 (pin 27) is on +5V.
issues.why_it_matters: A regulator supply pin may need to be tied to 3.3V even in a 5V-fed design. I could not confirm this against Realtek's reference schematic, hence low confidence.

issues.evidence: CH217A U1 VIN (pin 6) net contains only J1 VBUS and U1.6, with no capacitor. The CH217 datasheet says VIN should have an external capacitor of 10uF or more.
issues.why_it_matters: With no local input cap, hot-plug inductance from the host cable can ring above the 6V absolute maximum on VIN, and the current-limit loop may misbehave.

issues.evidence: The six +3V3 pins (11, 20, 23, 33, 39, 40) share only C9 and C10 (1u). Pins 11, 33, 39 and 40 are 5.8-9.6mm from the nearest cap. The six +1V0 pins share only C7 and C8 (1u). Pins 14, 19 and 34 are 4.7-6.7mm away. There are no 100nF caps per pin.
issues.why_it_matters: GbE PHY and USB3 SerDes rails need a local high-frequency bypass at each pin. Sparse, distant decoupling raises jitter, EMI and the risk of link errors.

issues.evidence: USB3 device-TX path: P = 1.54mm + 23.72mm = 25.26mm, N = 2.72mm + 23.85mm = 26.57mm, so about 1.3mm intra-pair mismatch (about 9ps). The other pairs match within 0.3mm.
issues.why_it_matters: This exceeds the tight intra-pair matching guidelines for 5Gbps (a few ps), but is only about 4% of the UI. It will probably work.

acceptable_designs.reason: 100nF AC-coupling caps are only on the device transmitter (U3SSTX to connector SSRX pins). The device receive pair (connector SSTX to U3SSRX) has no caps because the host's TX provides them, as the USB 3.0 spec requires. The TX/RX crossover and polarity are correct.

+3V3 is generated by the RTL8153B internal LDO (AVDD33 pin 20 is the LDO output), and DVDD10_UPS (pin 22) is an internal 1.0V LDO output that needs only C6. A missing external regulator on these rails is correct.
CH217A EN# is active-low. Tying it to GND keeps the switch always on, which is intended.
FLAG# is an optional open-drain fault output.
No external EEPROM or flash. The RTL8153B uses its eFuse autoload, and LED2/LANWAKEB are unused.
The RJ45 shield and Bob-Smith common go to GND through 1nF/2kV plus 1M. This is the standard chassis-to-logic-ground coupling.
CH217 Iset = 60k/Rset, so 62k gives about 0.97A, which suits a USB3 900mA port. The sheet note saying 24k-60k is only a guideline.
33pF per side with a 20pF-CL crystal gives about 16.5pF plus stray, which is close to 20pF. The datasheet allows CL 16-20pF (Realtek uses 27pF).
The small 'uncovered' spots on USB2 and MDI1 routes are only via anti-pads and connector pin clearances. The routes sit over solid In1/In4 GND planes.

[wrong] J1 is a USB-A plug (reverse polarity impossible); VBUS goes straight into U1 CH217A, a current-limited USB power switch (over-current/short/thermal protection), so a protection part does touch it.

notes: Checked the RTL8153B-VB pin functions against the Realtek datasheet Rev 1.4 (pins 20, 22, 25-28). Checked the CH217A pinout and Iset formula against the WCH datasheet V1.3. Diff pairs analysed with a script: length per layer, vias, and adjacent-plane coverage (GND on In1/In4). Not verified: the HR911130A pin-to-pair mapping and LED polarity (trusted the easyeda symbol), whether HC-USB3.0-C26 is a plug or a receptacle (no datasheet found), the RTL8153B QFN-40 EP size, and whether VDDREG33 must be tied in a 5V-fed design.
